topic: Advantages of Inclined Planes, Screws, and Wedges
key_concepts: Simple machines change the direction and size of forces
An inclined plane is a tilted flat surface used to raise or lower loads more easily
The input force on an inclined plane is the applied push or pull
The output force on an inclined plane equals the weight of the object
Mechanical advantage is the ratio of output force to input force
Mechanical advantage of an inclined plane equals length divided by height
Decreasing inclined plane height decreases the force needed to move an object up
A screw is an inclined plane wrapped around a cylinder
Mechanical advantage of a screw equals circumference divided by pitch
A wedge is two inclined planes combined with a common base
Mechanical advantage of a wedge equals length divided by thickness
Wedges can separate, split, cut, lift, or hold objects
